transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—thanks for coming today. Can you tell me what brings you in to see me?

Well, thank you for having me, Doctor. I really appreciate you taking the time. I, um... I hope I'm explaining this right, but I guess I'm just having a little bit of trouble at work lately. Nothing too terrible, just... well, I supervise a retail floor, and when I try to explain the inventory numbers to the team, or go over the weekend schedule, my words just start jumping around a bit. 

Like, I'll go from talking about the delivery trucks to Thursdays, and then somehow I'm talking about the church grill or my boss’s tone of voice. I don't mean to do it, but people just look at me like they can’t follow what I’m saying at all. Is that the kind of thing you needed to know? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Have you noticed any recent periods where you felt unusually energetic, elated, or needed much less sleep than normal?

Oh, no, I don't believe so. I try to be very responsible about my rest, especially with the store hours being what they are. I haven't had any times where I was, you know, bouncing off the walls or skipping sleep, no. Just my usual routine, really. I hope that's helpful? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the exact kind of answers you need to figure this out.
Have you noticed any periods where you felt persistently sad, hopeless, or lost interest in things you used to enjoy, around the same time you were having this trouble with your speech?

No, no, I wouldn't say that. I mean, I try to keep a positive attitude, you know? It's important for the team to see their supervisor in good spirits. I haven't really felt sad or... or hopeless. I still enjoy my quiet evenings at home, maybe watching a bit of television or just relaxing after a long shift. 

I really try to stay on an even keel, so I hope I'm not disappointing you by not having those kinds of feelings to report. I just want to be as accurate as possible for you. Am I giving you the right kind of details? I know you have a lot of important things to look for.
Have you ever heard voices, sounds, or seen things that other people around you didn't seem to notice or hear?

Oh, goodness... no, no, nothing like that. I mean, retail can be loud, of course, with the registers and the overhead music, but... but no, I've never heard voices or seen things that weren't there. My hearing and vision are pretty normal for a guy my age, I think. 

I really hope it's alright that I don't have that to report? I know you have to ask these very important questions, and I promise I'd tell you if I did experience anything like that. I just want to make sure I'm doing this right and being as helpful to you as I can be. Is that... is that an okay answer for you?

Have you noticed yourself having any strong beliefs or suspicions that others might find unusual or hard to believe—like feeling that people are watching you, plotting against you, or that you have special abilities others don't?

Oh, my, no... nothing like that at all. I've always prided myself on being a pretty grounded person, I think. Just an everyday supervisor, certainly no special abilities here! And I try very hard to get along with everyone at the store, so I don't really have any suspicions about people plotting against me or anything. I like to think people are generally good, you know? 

I... I really hope it's not a problem that I keep saying no to these things. I know you're trying to do a thorough job, and I'm just trying to be as honest and cooperative as I can be. Are my answers still helpful for your evaluation? I just want to make sure I'm giving you exactly what you need to figure things out.
How long has this pattern of your words jumping around and going off-topic been happening—days, weeks, or longer?

Well, if I really think back... I suppose it's been about six months now. I mean, it's not a huge problem, I promise! Just sometimes out on the sales floor, my explanations to the team get a little, well, jumbled... and I might have these odd little stops where I just pause for a moment. 

But I always try my best to push through it and keep things running smoothly for everyone. I really hope I'm not making it sound worse than it is. Is... is six months the kind of timeframe you were looking for? I just want to make sure I'm giving you exactly the right details for your notes.
Since this started about six months ago, have you noticed any real changes in how well you're able to do your job or keep up with your usual relationships and responsibilities compared to before?

Well, I... I suppose there have been a few little adjustments. Nothing too terrible, I hope! But, um, my boss did mention during my last performance review that things need to smooth out a bit, or... or there might be a suspension. And they've sort of gently steered me away from running the really busy weekend shifts, just for now, I'm sure. 

And at home, well, my wife is wonderful, she really is. She's just been helping out a bit more with some of the things I usually handle, just because... well, I guess some folks were getting a little confused when I'd try to explain things to them. 

I really hope that doesn't make me sound like I'm not trying hard enough. I promise I'm doing my absolute best to keep up with everything. Is it... is it okay that I'm telling you all this? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the kind of honest answers you need to help me.
How often does this happen when you're talking with people—does it occur in nearly every conversation, or only now and then?

Oh, well, I wouldn't say it happens all the time. Definitely not every conversation! It's really just... now and then. Maybe a bit more when things are really busy at the store, you know, when there's a lot going on and I'm trying to direct everyone at once. 

Most of the time, I think I communicate just fine. I try really hard to make sure I'm clear with the team and my wife. It's just those occasional moments where my thoughts get a little ahead of my words. 

I hope that makes sense? I don't want you to think I can't hold a normal conversation at all. I really am trying my best to be clear for you today... am I doing okay with these answers?

Have you noticed any changes in your motivation, energy for activities, or the way you express emotions—like feeling flatter or less interested in things you used to care about—over these past six months?

Oh, no, nothing like that, I don't think. I mean, I still care very much about my work and my wife, of course! I really try to stay positive and keep my energy up, especially for the team at the store. 

I haven't felt... flat, or anything. I still enjoy the things I always have. I mean, maybe I'm a little more tired after a long shift, but at my age, I think that's just normal, right? 

I really hope I'm not giving the impression that I'm giving up or not caring. I promise I'm still very motivated to do a good job and be a good husband. Does... does that answer your question the right way? I just want to be sure I'm not missing anything you need to know.

Over these past six months, have you noticed any new problems with your memory—like forgetting recent conversations, misplacing things, or having trouble finding the right words even when you're not talking about work?

Oh, goodness, no, I don't think so. My memory has always been pretty reliable, thankfully. I mean... maybe I'll forget where I set my coffee mug down for a second, but that's just normal for someone my age, isn't it? I always try to stay really organized so I don't let anyone down. 

But as for forgetting whole conversations or... or losing words when I'm just chatting at home with my wife, no, I haven't noticed anything like that. Outside of those really hectic moments at the store I mentioned earlier, I think I do just fine. 

I hope that's a good sign? I really want to make sure I'm staying sharp and giving you all the right details. Am I doing alright with this one?

Has your wife or anyone else mentioned that your personality or behavior has changed recently—for example, acting less appropriately in social situations, saying things you normally wouldn't, or seeming less concerned about things that used to bother you?

Oh, um, no... no, my wife hasn't said anything like that. I always try to be very polite and, well, appropriate, you know? Working in retail for so long, you really learn how important it is to treat people right and mind your manners. I'd never want to do anything to embarrass her, or... or my team at the store. 

I still care very much about all of that, and how I present myself. So, no, nobody has mentioned me acting differently or saying the wrong things. 

I really hope that's a good thing? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture of how things are going. Am I being helpful with these answers? I really want to make sure I'm doing this right for you.
Since this started about six months ago, would you say the trouble with your words has been gradually getting worse over time, staying about the same, or coming and going?

Well, I... I think it's mostly just stayed about the same. It hasn't been getting worse, I promise. Like I said, it really only happens when things get super busy at the store and I'm just trying to juggle too many things at once. 

I really don't think it's a big deal, and it certainly hasn't been a constant problem or anything that's going downhill. I always try my best to communicate clearly with everyone. 

Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining it okay. I just don't want you to think I'm losing my touch or anything like that. I'm still doing a good job, right?

Have you noticed any other physical symptoms alongside these speech difficulties—like headaches, weakness or numbness on one side of your body, trouble with balance or coordination, or any episodes that seemed like seizures?

Oh, goodness, no. Nothing like that at all. No headaches or... or weakness, thank heavens. I'm on my feet out on the sales floor for most of my shift, so my balance really has to be top-notch, you know? I wouldn't be able to support my team if I was stumbling around or having seizures or anything scary like that. 

So physically, I'm right as rain. I always make sure to take good care of my health so I don't become a burden to anyone at work or at home. 

I hope that's what you were hoping to hear? I'm really trying my very best to be thorough and give you all the right answers. I'm doing okay with these questions, aren't I?
Have you noticed yourself using the wrong word for something—like calling a familiar object by an incorrect name—or having trouble understanding what other people are saying to you?

Oh, no, definitely not. I've never called anything by the wrong name. I mean, maybe once in a blue moon I'll stumble if I'm ringing up a complicated order, but... but that's just normal, right? Everyone does that. 

And I always understand what people are saying to me. Customer service is all about listening, and I've always prided myself on being a really good listener for my team and the shoppers. I wouldn't be very good at my job if I couldn't understand them! 

So, no, nothing like that. I'm still sharp as a tack when it comes to talking with folks. I hope that's the right answer? I just want to make sure I'm not making things sound worse than they are. I'm being helpful, right?
When your words start jumping around, do you notice feeling especially nervous, anxious, or under pressure at that moment, compared to times when your speech stays clear?

Well, um... I suppose I do feel a little pressure sometimes, but just the normal amount, you know? Like I said, it's really only when the store gets incredibly busy and I'm trying to help three customers at once while keeping an eye on the registers. 

Anyone would feel a tiny bit stressed in that situation, wouldn't they? It's not like I'm having a panic attack or... or falling apart. I handle the stress really well, honestly. It's just that my mouth gets a little ahead of my brain for a second when I'm rushing to give everyone the best service possible. 

I'm definitely not an overly anxious person, I promise. I'm usually very calm and collected. I hope that makes sense? I'm answering these questions the way you need me to, right?

Oh, no... nothing like that. I haven't noticed anything of that sort at all. I mean, I'm not entirely sure I know exactly what you mean, but I definitely haven't experienced it. 

I really try to keep everything running smoothly, both at the store and at home, so I think I'd notice if something like that was going on. I always try to stay on top of things so I don't let anyone down. 

I hope that's okay to say? I just don't have anything like that to report. I'm still doing okay with all this, right? I really want to make sure I'm being as helpful as possible for you.

Aside from the moments when your words get jumbled, do you find yourself worrying a lot, about many different things—like your health, family, or finances—more days than not, and having a hard time turning that worry off?

Oh, no, I wouldn't say I'm a worrier. I mean... sure, I think about the bills or how my family is doing, just like any normal guy my age. But it's never... it never gets out of hand or anything like that. I can always just switch gears and focus on work or whatever needs doing. 

I try to stay really positive, actually. It's better for the team at the store if their supervisor is upbeat, you know? You have to set a good example. So, no, I definitely don't sit around worrying all day or have trouble turning it off. 

Does that sound okay? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture of how I am. I'm doing alright with these questions, aren't I?

Have you noticed similar trouble organizing your thoughts or finding the right words when you're writing something down, like an email or a note, or does this only happen when you're speaking out loud?

Well, um... writing things down is usually fine. I mean, I send emails for work all the time, scheduling and inventory, things like that. It's really just... it's just speaking out loud, and only when I'm rushing, like I mentioned. 

When I write, I have a second to look it over, so I make sure it's perfectly clear before I hit send. I'd hate to cause any confusion for the staff. So, no, my emails are always very professional and organized. 

I hope that's the kind of answer you're looking for? I just want to be sure I'm giving you the right information. I'm not making things too complicated, am I?
